Maya: Heads-up — OrbitIQ just sent a Q4 draft commit request: 50,000 GPU-hours across the quarter with a 20% burst allowance. They want 95p latency <250ms and can’t tolerate cold-starts. Can infra run sizing + cost delta vs on-demand?

Kevin: Need workload profile before we size. avg seq len? peak concurrency? is that 50k for the whole Q or monthly?

Sabrina: From the call notes — it’s 50k GPU-hours for Q4 (Oct–Dec). Baseline traffic ~8k sessions/day, avg seq ~512 tokens, ~90% generation. Peak concurrency observed ~275 req/s historically. They’re projecting a holiday multiplier of ~2.5x for weeks 48–52.

Anil: Quick back-of-envelope sizing (assuming 50k GPU-hrs for the quarter):
```
# rough math (Q4 = 3 months ≈ 2160 hours)
50_000 GPU-hrs / 2160 hrs ≈ 23.15 average GPUs across Q4
avg GPUs ≈ 23 -> with 20% burst => ~27.8 -> round to 28 GPUs
Peak weeks *2.5 => short spikes may require ~70 GPUs unless burst window limited
```
So we’d need a plan: base 24 GPUs reserved, burst pool up to 70 for short windows, or push more caching/batching during peak to reduce GPU demand.

Lucas: Agree. Also region constraint: OrbitIQ requires EU data residency but wants failover to US-west. We can’t allocate Dedicated GPUs across regions without separate capacity pools. That means either split their commit (EU + US) or accept a lower SLA on failover. Splitting will increase overall commit size because of lower utilization.

Maya: Sabrina — did they insist on a single-region commit?

Sabrina: They want primary in EU and DR in US-west. From negotiating standpoint they prefer one contract but will consider two-line-item commits if cost delta is <8%.

Kevin: Two options to present: 1) Single EU commit sized for peak with regional fallback to US on overflow (best latency but higher cost). 2) Split commit: EU primary + small DR in US (higher management overhead, slightly higher combined hours). Also need to be explicit about buffer policy — our standard is 15% burst allowance for Dedicated; they asked for 20%.

Anil: Cost delta quick calc assuming commit price $0.60/GPU-hr vs on-demand $0.95:
```
(0.95-0.60) * 50_000 ≈ $17,500 saved vs on-demand across Q4
```
If we add a second small DR commit of 5k hrs in US, net commit = 55k hrs -> commit discount scales slightly but still savings >$19k.

Maya: Ops question — can SRE guarantee the short burst windows? We can’t keep ephemeral capacity unused for months. We need a ramp/rate plan in the contract (e.g., allowed bursts up to 2 weeks per quarter) and stricter charge for reserved but unused capacity.

Kevin: From infra side: we can support a rolling ramp: 25% in month1, 50% in month2, 100% in month3, with scheduled forecasting checkpoints. For holiday weeks we put a temporary autoscale override for 7–14 days. Need customer to commit to dates 30 days in advance for capacity locking.

Sabrina: OrbitIQ prefers flexibility but can give 30d notice for major holiday spikes. They want a soft guarantee without heavy penalties.

Lucas: Network note — cross-region failover will add egress / inter-region replication cost. Rough network estimate: 20TB/month replication -> ~$3k–6k/month depending on path and peer. Call out in doc.

Anil: Risks: 1) If peaks exceed forecast and we can’t burst, we fallback to lower-tier models -> degraded quality. 2) If they want single-contract cross-region guarantee, we need to mark capacity as dual-reserved which has higher opportunity cost.

Maya: Proposed negotiation points to present to OrbitIQ:
- Base commit 40k GPU-hrs in EU + 10k optional DR in US (total 50k with opt-in), 15% standard burst included, 20% as paid option at +10% fee.
- Ramp schedule (25%/50%/100%) and 30d advance for planned holiday spikes; 7–14d short bursts allowed with extra charge beyond free burst cap.
- Pricing: commit rate $0.60/hr (EU), DR rate $0.62/hr (US) with on-demand fallback at $0.95/hr.
- SLA: 95p latency target with explicit fallback policies to smaller models during capacity exhaustion.
- Network/replication fee line item (estimate) and optional managed replication.

Sabrina: That looks good. OrbitIQ will want the math in a single doc and the exact dates they can request bursts. I’ll push for the 20% free burst as a negotiation ask.

Kevin: Action items:
- @Anil: produce a 3-month hourly capacity plan + cost scenarios (single EU vs split) by EOD tomorrow.
- @Lucas: estimate cross-region egress + replication cost and any infra-level constraints.
- @Maya: draft contract language for ramp/burst clauses and optional paid burst.
- @Sabrina: reconfirm the holiday weeks & ask for preferred DR latency targets.
